title: He gave them the cup…
paragraphs:
He gave them the cup…
before the blood was even spilled.
Sit with that.
Because most of us think God waits.

Waits until you fix yourself.
Waits until you stop the habit.
Waits until you become “worthy enough.”

But in that upper room—while betrayal was already breathing—Jesus lifted the bread and said, “This is my body given for you.”
Then the cup—“This is the new covenant in my blood.” (Luke 22:19–20)

Future blood.
Present promise.
And that’s where it gets uncomfortable.

Because some of us are still delaying obedience, saying, “Lord, I’ll come back when I’m clean.”
Some of us are worshipping on Sunday but negotiating with sin on Monday.
Some of us look spiritual… but we’re tired, secretly compromised, slowly drifting.
Let me ask you something:

What are you still hiding that Jesus already paid for?
What are you postponing that heaven already settled?
Because here’s the truth we don’t like:

You are not waiting on God.
God is waiting on your surrender.
Read that again.

The disciples at that table weren’t flawless.
Peter was hours away from denial.
The others would scatter in fear.
And Judas?
Already decided.

Yet Jesus still passed the bread.
Still offered the cup.
Why?

Because covenant was never based on their performance.
It was anchored in His sacrifice.
This is the AHA moment:
The promise came before the proof—because the proof was never about you.
Let that hit.

Romans 5:8 says that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
Not after.
Not when you improved.
Not when you became consistent.
While.

That means Jesus looked at your worst day—
your hidden sin, your pride, your relapse, your silent rebellion—
and still said,

“I will give My body for that.
I will shed My blood for that.”
And here’s the spiritual mirror you can’t ignore:
If you keep running from God because of your sin, you are rejecting the very reason He came.

That’s not humility.
That’s unbelief dressed as shame.

Some scholars interpret the Last Supper as both a remembrance and a prophetic declaration—Jesus announcing what would secure eternal forgiveness (Matthew 26:28).
Meaning this wasn’t just a meal.

It was a warning.
And an invitation.
The warning?
You can sit at the table… and still miss the Savior.
Judas did.
Let that disturb you.
Because proximity to Jesus is not the same as surrender to Jesus.

Church attendance.
Worship songs.
Christian captions.
None of it replaces repentance.
Here’s the conviction edge:
You can look like a disciple and still live like a stranger to the cross.
But here’s where grace walks in.

The same Jesus who knew betrayal was coming… still broke bread.
The same Savior who saw denial in Peter… still called him “mine.”
The same Lord who sees your hidden battles right now… is still offering you covenant.
Not later.
Now.

Hebrews 9:22 reminds us that without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.
And Jesus didn’t hesitate.

He went to the cross.
Fully.
Willingly.
For you.

Sin is real.
It separates.
It corrupts.
But the Gospel?
Stronger.

Jesus Christ lived the life you couldn’t live, died the death you deserved, and rose again so you could be forgiven, made new, and brought into covenant with God—not by works, but by grace through faith (Ephesians 2:8–9).
So what now?

Stop waiting to be worthy.
Start responding to what’s already been given.

Repent.
Not just feel bad—turn back.
Surrender the secret thing.
Drop the pride.
Come out of hiding.
Because the table is still set.
And the invitation still stands.
Not hype. Real growth.
Stay close.
And next time, we’re going deeper into the moment after the table—where silence in the garden revealed who truly understood the cup.
Don’t miss it.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
